newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets up commission to trace Nazi wealth.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets up commission to trace Nazi wealth.

text.p: Brazil on Monday set up a commission to trace gold and cash stolen from victims of the Holocaust which fugitive Nazis were believed to have smuggled into the country after the Second World War.
"We're not just talking about Jews and Germans. We're talking about (Brazilians) who don't want to be a part of these acts," President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said after setting up the commission.
Between 1,200 and 1,500 Nazis were thought to have sought refuge in Brazil after the war, bringing with them the wealth of Jews who perished in concentration camps.

Jewish investigators have said they believe Brazilian authorities turned a blind eye to the Nazis and that their fortunes were deposited back into the Swiss banks from where they were originally stolen.
Argentina, which was another favourite destination for Nazis on the run, in November sent documents from its Central Bank to the Los Angeles-based Simon Wiesenthal Centre, which hunts war criminals.
One of the Brazilian commission's first jobs will be to study the accounts of federal bank Banco do Brasil which acted as Brazil's Central Bank during the post-war period.
It will also investigate the possibility that Brazilian officials were bribed by Nazis to allow them into the country.

"Brazil lived a long way from World War Two and a lot of Brazilians do not know of the horrors that took place," said Henry Sobel, the senior rabbi of Sao Paulo's Jewish Congregation, Brazil's biggest Jewish group.

Sobel has been pressing the Brazilian government to open up its banking records to compliment an ongoing investigation by the World Jewish Congress into Swiss banks and their alleged collaboration with Nazi Germany.
